title: Iodine as the second target: what DAMA/LIBRA's modulation data and COSINE/ANAIS already say about an inelastic 300-390 keV splitting
question: What unmodulated rate S0 and DAMA-style modulation amplitude S_m does LZ's one-event inelastic best fit (1 TeV, delta = 300/350/366/380 keV) predict in NaI(Tl) keVee bins (Q_I = 0.09), how do they compare with DAMA/LIBRA's measured amplitudes and the COSINE-100/ANAIS-112 nulls, and what NaI exposure would be needed?
headline_result: TeV inelastic DM at LZ's one-event fit predicts a June-phased NaI(Tl) modulation amplitude of 3.5e-8 to 2.1e-7 cpd/kg/keV at 15-33 keVee, 7e3-4e4 below DAMA/LIBRA's per-bin sensitivity of 1.5e-3 and zero below 8.7 keVee; for delta >= 350 keV the signal is a non-sinusoidal spike (S_m/S0 = 1.3-1.9); no NaI experiment constrains or could reproduce it, and NaI needs 2e8-8e9 t yr (DAMA-like) or 21-390 t yr (background-free) to see the modulation vs 12-15 t yr to count 3 events
key_numbers: windows 8.7-67.0/15.1-52.6/18.7-46.4/24.2-38.7 keVee (delta 300/350/366/380); Na blind (delta_max 76 keV); I/Xe 0.589/0.296/0.143/0.023 (=P015); window S0 5.4-6.7e-7 cpd/kg NaI, 0.20-0.25 ev/(t yr); DAMA 2.46 t yr 0.53-0.61 events among 1-5e7 counts; S_m peak 3.5e-8/8.0e-8/1.05e-7/2.1e-7 cpd/kg/keV at 15.5/19.5/32.5/31.5 keVee (DAMA resolution -17 to -35%); S_m/S0 0.46/1.27/1.59/1.87; A2/A1 0.06/0.28/0.48/0.81; zero-rate fraction 0/0/0.33/0.66; phase 151.9 d; DAMA sigma(S_m) 1.49e-3 (1 keVee, B=1), sigma/S_m 4.2e4/1.9e4/1.4e4/7.1e3, all-bins z 0.5-3e-4; 8-16 keVee DAMA bin 0.0004+-0.0005 vs 1.5e-8; COSINE/ANAIS sigma 7-9e-3; E_3sigma DAMA-like 2.6e8-8e9 t yr; bkg-free modulation 390/57/29/21 t yr; 3 events 14.0/15.2/12.2/12.2 t yr NaI; Q_I 0.06-0.12 rescales windows ~Q, amplitudes ~1/Q
model_or_mechanism: O1 isoscalar inelastic DM (WimPyDD 127I shell-model response, LZ unit coupling per P003), normalised to LZ 1 event as in P015; Baxter-2021 halo with Earth motion on 73 days via per-stream kernels; constant iodine quenching; Fourier decomposition of the annual rate; Poisson cosine-amplitude sensitivity sigma_Sm = sqrt(2B/(exposure dE))
confidence: high (rates reproduce P015 and WimPyDD's own DAMA target; the 1e4 gap dwarfs the recalled-input uncertainties)
agent_tools: Read x22, Bash x16, Write x5, Edit x19, Skill x1 (dataviz)
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1 (erf/erfc); matplotlib 3.11.2; WimPyDD 2.0.4 (eft_hamiltonian, streamed_halo_function by day, diff_rate per-stream kernels on I/Xe, DAMA_LIBRA_2019 target + bundled quenching/resolution/S_m tables); common/lzcommon.py
